  PROBLEM: Case-sensitive matching skips lowercase or mixed-case secret-named environment variables, so their values are not masked and may be emitted in workflow logs.
  WHY: If Codex echoes a short or non-token-shaped secret to stderr, it can reach `codex-stderr-tail line=` or `captured_path_error=` unmasked; reviewers disagreed on severity (MAJOR vs BLOCKER), so the highest severity is used.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The values of secret-named env vars are masked before `security_audit_sanitize_log_value`, with no case qualification.
  expected_change_site: scripts/security_audit.sh: security_audit_mask_stderr_line
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `case "${secret_env_name}" in` matches uppercase-only patterns without case normalization; lowercase or mixed-case names fall through to `*) continue`.
- requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: Existing fixtures use uppercase-named environment variables only; no regression test sets a lowercase or mixed-case secret-named variable and asserts its value is absent from emitted stderr tail and `captured_path_error=` output.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:123-124 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Bash `case` glob patterns are case-sensitive, so lowercase or mixed-case secret-shaped environment variable names fall through without extracting or masking their values.
  WHY: If Codex echoes a short or non-token-shaped secret to stderr, it can reach workflow log output unmasked.

- Requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value" (PR description checklist item 3, agents.md note at line 2175, changelog fragment line 5).
  Expected change site: tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py, alongside the existing secret-masking tests (test_security_audit_codex_stderr_tail_masks_short_secrets_and_unpadded_base64, test_security_audit_codex_stderr_masks_each_line_of_multiline_secrets)
  Evidence of absence: Every existing fixture uses an uppercase-named env var (SHORT_API_KEY at line 1098, MULTILINE_SECRET at line 1121, test-openrouter-key and test-token in the 402 test). No test exports a lowercase or mixed-case name such as api_key, client_secret, auth_token, or db_password and asserts the value is absent from codex-stderr-tail line= and captured_path_error= output. The case-sensitivity fix to security_audit_mask_stderr_line has no automated regression coverage.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: lines 123-129 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The case statement matching secret-named environment variable names uses case-sensitive glob patterns without case normalization, skipping lowercase and mixed-case names.
  WHY: If Codex echoes a short or non-standard secret value to stderr, it can appear unmasked in `captured_path_error=` and `codex-stderr-tail line=` log lines.

- Requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value" (agents.md note at line 2175, changelog.d/5785-security-audit-codex-stderr-tail.md line 5, PR description checklist item 3).
  Expected change site: tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py alongside test_security_audit_codex_stderr_tail_masks_short_secrets_and_unpadded_base64
  Evidence of absence: All secret environment variable fixtures in tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py only define uppercase variable names (SHORT_API_KEY, MULTILINE_SECRET, OPENROUTER_API_KEY). No regression test verifies that values from lowercase or mixed-case secret environment variables (such as api_key or client_secret) are masked from emitted stderr tail and diagnostic output.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: `security_audit_mask_stderr_line`, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in *TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*|PAT|*_PAT|PAT_*|*_PAT_*` statement (the round-6 hunk around lines 123-129 of the post-round-6 file). | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Case-sensitive matching skips lowercase or mixed-case secret-named environment variables, leaving short or non-token-shaped values unmasked if Codex echoes them to stderr.
  WHY: The function does not read the value for names such as `client_secret`, so a stderr line containing that value may be printed verbatim into the GitHub Actions log.

- Requirement: "the values of secret-named env vars (a multiline value line by line; a value or line under 8 characters only where it stands as a whole word) are masked before security_audit_sanitize_log_value" (PR description checklist item 3, agents.md note at line 2175, changelog.d/5785-security-audit-codex-stderr-tail.md line 5, the function-level comment at scripts/security_audit.sh:80-94, and Copilot review comment 4154966986 which says "Normalize the variable name for this check while continuing to read the original name's value"). No case qualification appears in any of these declarations.
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh inside `security_audit_mask_stderr_line`, the `case "${secret_env_name}" in` statement at the top of the `while IFS= read -r secret_env_name; do … done < <(compgen -e)` loop; the value read must still use the original name (`"${!secret_env_name-}"`).
  Evidence of absence: The case statement at scripts/security_audit.sh line 123-129 matches `secret_env_name` directly against uppercase-only glob patterns (`*TOKEN*|*API_KEY*|*SECRET*|*PASSWORD*|PAT|*_PAT|PAT_*|*_PAT_*`) without case normalization (e.g. `"${secret_env_name^^}"`). All four documented contract sources (PR description, agents.md, changelog fragment, function-level comment) state the guarantee in case-neutral terms, so a case-sensitive implementation is a contract violation against the deliverable.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- Requirement: Regression coverage for a lowercase or mixed-case secret-named environment variable whose value reaches Codex stderr and is asserted absent from the emitted `codex-stderr-tail line=` and `captured_path_error=` output (Copilot review comment 4154966986 says "add a short-secret regression case"; the cross-pollination consensus task gap repeats this).
  Expected change site: tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py alongside the existing secret-masking tests (`test_security_audit_codex_failure_prints_masked_stderr_tail_with_provider_402`, `test_security_audit_codex_stderr_tail_masks_short_secrets_and_unpadded_base64`, `test_security_audit_codex_stderr_masks_each_line_of_multiline_secrets`, `test_security_audit_codex_path_diagnostic_masks_secrets_on_path_error_line`).
  Evidence of absence: Every existing fixture sets an uppercase-named env var (`SHORT_API_KEY`, `MULTILINE_SECRET`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `test-openrouter-key`, `test-token`, `OPENROUTER_PROMPT_FILE` is a file not a secret). No test sets a lowercase or mixed-case name such as `api_key`, `client_secret`, `auth_token`, `db_password`, or `My_Api_Key` and asserts the value is absent from the emitted stderr. The fix to `security_audit_mask_stderr_line` therefore has no automated coverage without this test.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
